items.label: f09-illustrative-fake-code
items.front: The lab labels some snippets "Illustrative fake code". What does that label tell you?
items.back: The snippet is a skeleton showing a test's shape, not a real test: names in it may not exist in the repo. The real tests live at the file:line paths the workout cites, so open those to check actual behaviour.

items.label: f08-service-workout-anatomy
items.front: What is the arrange / act / assert shape of the lab's service rejection workouts?
items.back: Arrange: a ServiceContext for the actor under test (built from a seeded workspace with a ctx helper) plus an input. Act: call the service verb directly, with no router or HTTP in between. Assert: `await expect(...).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(SomeError)` for the expected error class.

items.label: f01-test-layers
items.front: In the test-first lab, what does a router test prove that a service test does not, and what should it not repeat?
items.back: A router test proves the public API contract: that service rejections reach clients as the right TRPCError code (NotFoundError becomes NOT_FOUND) and that the procedure works end to end. It should not re-assert every association the service tests already cover.

items.label: f03-get-events-shape
items.front: What does getEvents return, and which event types and statuses can it produce?
items.back: One list of events in a common shape { id, name, from, to, type, status }: maintenances (type maintenance, status info), incidents for non-static components (type incident, name Downtime, status error), and status reports (type report, status success if resolved, otherwise degraded).

items.label: f04-router-create-return
items.front: What does the tRPC statusReport.create return, according to the router workout?
items.back: Not the report itself: it returns the initial status_report_update row with the caller's notifySubscribers flag spread into it ({ ...initialUpdate, notifySubscribers }), the shape the dashboard consumes. A caller that did not send the flag sees notifySubscribers undefined.

items.label: f06-load-seeded-workspace
items.front: What does the `loadSeededWorkspace` test helper do?
items.back: It loads a seeded workspace row (by default id 1, the team-plan fixture) and parses it with selectWorkspaceSchema; if the row is missing it throws, asking whether the db was seeded.

items.label: f02-ssrf-table
items.front: Which categories of hostile input do the SSRF tests cover, and what testing pattern do they teach?
items.back: Allowed public URLs; blocked protocols (ftp, file, gopher, javascript, data); private IPv4; private hostnames (localhost, metadata hosts); private and IPv4-mapped IPv6; invalid URLs; the async variant. Pattern: a table of hostile examples looped into one it() per case, because safety code needs many bad inputs, not one happy path.

items.label: f07-kata-shape
items.front: What shape does each kata in the lab's test-design katas follow?
items.back: A feature premise; existing facts, each with a file:line cite into the real code; a test to write first (marked illustrative fake code); then the expected first failure, a design question, or the expected learning to check yourself against.

items.label: f05-test-surfaces
items.front: Name the lab's four test surfaces by file glob, and what each kind of test covers.
items.back: packages/api/src/router/*.test.ts: tRPC router behaviour, procedure calls, error codes, cross-workspace guards. packages/services/src/**/__tests__/*.test.ts: reusable domain services, transactions, scopes, notifications. packages/utils/src/*.test.ts: pure utilities and safety helpers. apps/**/src/lib/**/*.test.ts: app-specific helpers and proxy/domain logic.

items.prompt: In the test map's illustrative service-test skeleton, what does the test pass to `expectAuditRow` to identify the audit row it expects?

choices.text: Only the entity id, read from the committed database once the test ends
Workspace id, action, entity type and entity id, read through the test's tx
A full row snapshot and its timestamp, compared after the transaction commits
The action name alone, captured by a logging spy registered on globalThis

choices: Only the entity id, read from the committed database once the test ends
Workspace id, action, entity type and entity id, read through the test's tx
A full row snapshot and its timestamp, compared after the transaction commits
The action name alone, captured by a logging spy registered on globalThis

items.explanation: 01-test-map lines 54-60: the skeleton calls expectAuditRow({ workspaceId, action: 'thing.create', entityType: 'thing', entityId: result.id, db: tx }), and line 43 says the helper asserts audit rows were written. The read goes through the same tx the service wrote in; that transaction is always rolled back (line 37), so nothing is ever read after a commit, and no snapshot or log spy is involved.

items.prompt: notifyStatusReport runs for a workspace whose plan has limits['status-subscribers'] set to false. What happens?

choices.text: It throws ForbiddenError, as the plan lacks subscriber support
It dispatches the update, as plan limits apply only in the UI
It returns quietly without dispatching anything to subscribers
It queues the dispatch until the workspace upgrades its plan

choices: It throws ForbiddenError, as the plan lacks subscriber support
It dispatches the update, as plan limits apply only in the UI
It returns quietly without dispatching anything to subscribers
It queues the dispatch until the workspace upgrades its plan

items.explanation: After checking that the update belongs to the workspace, the function does if (!ctx.workspace.limits['status-subscribers']) return; before dispatchStatusReportUpdate. The comment says the silent skip matches emailRouter.sendStatusReport. ForbiddenError is thrown only when the update belongs to another workspace.

items.prompt: Service Workout 3's extension asks for the read-only test again, this time with a `makeMcpCtx` actor holding only the `read` scope. What should that test expect from a write verb, and why?

choices.text: ForbiddenError, as requireScope checks mcp actors the same way as apiKey ones
ForbiddenError, as requireScope rejects every non-user actor regardless of scope
NotFoundError, as an mcp actor's read scope hides the page it targets
Success, as requireScope checks scopes only for apiKey actors, not mcp ones

choices: ForbiddenError, as requireScope checks mcp actors the same way as apiKey ones
ForbiddenError, as requireScope rejects every non-user actor regardless of scope
NotFoundError, as an mcp actor's read scope hides the page it targets
Success, as requireScope checks scopes only for apiKey actors, not mcp ones

items.explanation: Service Workout 3: the existing test gives makeApiKeyCtx scopes ['read'] and expects ForbiddenError (line 63); the real authorization function checks apiKey and mcp actors (line 65), and the extension exists 'since requireScope treats mcp like apiKey' (line 78). In require-scope.ts any other actor type returns early, and an apiKey/mcp actor that holds the required scope passes, so it is scope-based, not a blanket rejection.

items.prompt: Workout 1 lists what createStatusReport writes on the happy path. Besides the status_report row, which rows does it create?

choices.text: An update row, a page-component link row, and two audit rows
An update row only, with the audit rows written by a later job
A page-component link row and one audit row for the report
An update row and a subscriber notification row for each user

choices: An update row, a page-component link row, and two audit rows
An update row only, with the audit rows written by a later job
A page-component link row and one audit row for the report
An update row and a subscriber notification row for each user

items.explanation: The workout's behaviour block: status_report, status_report_update (the initial update), status_report_to_page_component (the association), and audit rows for the report and the update. Subscriber notification is a separate notifyStatusReport call, and audit is written in the same transaction, not later.

items.prompt: The test map's layer table assigns `getEvents` to a plain unit test. Which reason does the table give?

choices.text: It is a utility boundary that guards outbound URLs against SSRF
It is where the business rule for workspace ownership lives
It computes the public read model inside the statusPage.get call
It is a pure-ish helper that computes events over plain arrays

choices: It is a utility boundary that guards outbound URLs against SSRF
It is where the business rule for workspace ownership lives
It computes the public read model inside the statusPage.get call
It is a pure-ish helper that computes events over plain arrays

items.explanation: 01-test-map line 31: pure event computation is best tested with a unit test because getEvents is a pure-ish helper over arrays. The other reasons belong to other rows of the same table: the SSRF guard is a utility boundary (line 32), workspace ownership is a business rule in the service (line 30), and statusPage.get computing the public read model is a router/integration test (line 33).

items.prompt: pastDays is 45. A maintenance started 60 days ago, and an unresolved report's first update is also 60 days old. Which of them does getEvents include?

choices.text: Both, as getEvents applies no age limit to any of its event types
Only the report; maintenances older than the threshold are dropped
Only the maintenance, since reports must be updated within 45 days
Neither, as both start before the 45-day threshold for the feed

choices: Both, as getEvents applies no age limit to any of its event types
Only the report; maintenances older than the threshold are dropped
Only the maintenance, since reports must be updated within 45 days
Neither, as both start before the 45-day threshold for the feed

items.explanation: The maintenance loop returns early when maintenance.from < pastThreshod, and incidents check createdAt the same way. The reports branch deliberately skips the threshold; its comment says all unresolved reports are displayed. So the old report stays and the old maintenance goes.

items.prompt: The lab's test map names five helpers that construct `ServiceContext` actors for service tests. Which caller kinds do they model?

choices.text: User, API key, admin, Slack and guest actors
User, OAuth app, MCP, Slack and webhook actors
User, API key, MCP, Slack and inbound-webhook actors
User, API key, MCP, Slack and system-job actors

choices: User, API key, admin, Slack and guest actors
User, OAuth app, MCP, Slack and webhook actors
User, API key, MCP, Slack and inbound-webhook actors
User, API key, MCP, Slack and system-job actors

items.explanation: 01-test-map line 41: makeUserCtx, makeApiKeyCtx, makeMcpCtx, makeSlackCtx and makeSystemCtx construct ServiceContext actors. In helpers.ts (lines 121-204) they build actors of type user, apiKey, mcp, slack and system, the last one carrying a job name. The map has no webhook, admin, guest or OAuth-app constructor.

items.prompt: Service Workout 2 expects `NotFoundError` when a free-plan workspace tries to create a report on the team workspace's page. Why does the workout put this test at the service layer?

choices.text: Router callers need a live session, so tRPC tests cannot build one inside a test file
Only the service queries the page by id and workspace, so the rejection lives there
A database foreign key rejects the insert, and only service tests can reach that point
A requireScope check enforces workspace ownership, and it lives in the service

choices: Router callers need a live session, so tRPC tests cannot build one inside a test file
Only the service queries the page by id and workspace, so the rejection lives there
A database foreign key rejects the insert, and only service tests can reach that point
A requireScope check enforces workspace ownership, and it lives in the service

items.explanation: Service Workout 2, line 45: this belongs in service tests because the service owns the workspace page lookup (create.ts selects the page by id AND workspaceId and throws NotFoundError before any insert). Router tests do build callers, with createInnerTRPCContext (router Workout 1); requireScope only checks API-key and MCP scopes and runs before the lookup, so it is not what rejects a foreign page.

items.prompt: According to the lab's test map, what does the `withTestTransaction` helper do with the rows a service test writes?

choices.text: It wraps the test body in a transaction that always rolls the writes back
It rolls them back only when the test body fails one of its assertions
It commits them so the following tests can reuse the rows it inserted
It commits them, then a teardown hook deletes the rows by their test prefix

choices: It wraps the test body in a transaction that always rolls the writes back
It rolls them back only when the test body fails one of its assertions
It commits them so the following tests can reuse the rows it inserted
It commits them, then a teardown hook deletes the rows by their test prefix

items.explanation: 01-test-map line 37: withTestTransaction wraps a test body and always rolls back writes. In helpers.ts the callback runs inside db.transaction and then throws a private RollbackSignal, which the helper swallows, so the transaction never commits whether the assertions pass or fail; no teardown deletion or cross-test reuse is involved.

items.prompt: Kata 5 writes a test-first `expectAuditRow` check for the `status_report_update.create` row. What does the kata say a learner should take away about audit?

choices.text: Audit is a dashboard feature, so its test belongs with the UI components
Audit is a service-owned side effect, tied to the domain writes it records
Audit is a router concern, emitted only when calls arrive through tRPC
Audit is written by a later job, so the test must wait for it to commit

choices: Audit is a dashboard feature, so its test belongs with the UI components
Audit is a service-owned side effect, tied to the domain writes it records
Audit is a router concern, emitted only when calls arrive through tRPC
Audit is written by a later job, so the test must wait for it to commit

items.explanation: Kata 5 line 125: audit is not a UI feature; it is a service-owned side effect tied to domain writes. Line 109 places the emission in createStatusReport itself (create.ts lines 82-95 call emitAudit on the same tx as the inserts), so it is neither a later job nor something only the tRPC router emits.

items.prompt: getEvents is called with both pageComponentId and monitorId. How does it choose which maintenances to include?

choices.text: By both, keeping only maintenances that match the two at once
By either one, keeping maintenances that match pageComponentId or monitorId
By monitorId alone, since it is the older, backward-compatible key
By pageComponentId alone, with monitorId used only when it is absent

choices: By both, keeping only maintenances that match the two at once
By either one, keeping maintenances that match pageComponentId or monitorId
By monitorId alone, since it is the older, backward-compatible key
By pageComponentId alone, with monitorId used only when it is absent

items.explanation: The filter checks if (pageComponentId) first and returns its match; the monitorId branch runs only when pageComponentId is falsy, and with neither every maintenance is kept. The comment calls monitorId the backward-compatibility fallback.

items.prompt: Kata 3 targets the dashboard's status-reports page. What does that page render today while its reports or page query has no data yet?

choices.text: It throws to the nearest error boundary, which shows a retry button
It returns null, so the user sees a blank page until data arrives
It shows an empty table with a message saying there are no reports
It renders the layout's prefetched list, so no loading state is needed

choices: It throws to the nearest error boundary, which shows a retry button
It returns null, so the user sees a blank page until data arrives
It shows an empty table with a message saying there are no reports
It renders the layout's prefetched list, so no loading state is needed

items.explanation: Kata 3 (lines 62-66): the premise is that the dashboard should not return blank UI while the reports/page query state is unknown, and the existing fact is that the page currently returns null if reports or page is absent (page.tsx line 54: if (!statusReports || !page) return null). The layout's prefetch exists (line 68) but the page still returns null whenever data is missing; nothing throws or renders an empty table.

items.prompt: assertSafeUrl's docblock says it checks the resolved IP address. A public hostname whose DNS record points to 10.0.0.5 is passed in. What happens?

choices.text: It is allowed, as the code never resolves the hostname via DNS
It throws 'Invalid URL', since a private target is not a URL
It is blocked once a DNS lookup resolves the name to 10.0.0.5
It is blocked, since every hostname is first matched to an allowlist

choices: It is allowed, as the code never resolves the hostname via DNS
It throws 'Invalid URL', since a private target is not a URL
It is blocked once a DNS lookup resolves the name to 10.0.0.5
It is blocked, since every hostname is first matched to an allowlist

items.explanation: Despite the docblock and the test comment 'async, with DNS resolution', assertSafeUrl only parses the URL, checks http/https, and calls isBlockedHost on the hostname string. There is no lookup, so a public name pointing at a private address passes. The code is keyed, not the comment; this is an open SSRF gap (DNS rebinding as well).

items.prompt: The dashboard calls the tRPC statusReport.list with { pageId, statuses: ['resolved'] }. Which reports come back?

choices.text: Reports of every status, as the router sends the service statuses: []
Only resolved ones, but capped at 100 by the service's limit
Only resolved reports, since the service filters on statuses
None at all, since an unknown input key makes zod throw an error

choices: Reports of every status, as the router sends the service statuses: []
Only resolved ones, but capped at 100 by the service's limit
Only resolved reports, since the service filters on statuses
None at all, since an unknown input key makes zod throw an error

items.explanation: The router's zod object declares only period, order and pageId, so the extra key is stripped by default, and the call passes a fixed statuses: [], limit: 10_000, offset: 0. listStatusReports adds a status condition only when statuses.length > 0. The 100 cap belongs to the separate Connect handler. The guide says this test would fail today.

items.prompt: A dashboard user calls statusReport.create with a pageId from another workspace. Which tRPC error code reaches the client?

choices.text: BAD_REQUEST, as the input schema rejects the pageId
NOT_FOUND, translated from the service's NotFoundError
INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, since the insert hits a FK error
FORBIDDEN, as the page belongs to a different workspace

choices: BAD_REQUEST, as the input schema rejects the pageId
NOT_FOUND, translated from the service's NotFoundError
INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, since the insert hits a FK error
FORBIDDEN, as the page belongs to a different workspace

items.explanation: The service selects the page by id AND workspaceId and throws NotFoundError('page', ...) when nothing matches; toTRPCError maps the NOT_FOUND ServiceError code to TRPCError NOT_FOUND. The router test pins exactly that. No insert is attempted, and the id is a valid number for the schema.

items.prompt: statusPage.get sorts reports with a comparator meant to put reports without updates first. What is wrong with it when only b has no updates?

choices.text: It throws, as it reads the last update of an empty array
It returns 0, leaving the two reports in their original order
It returns -1, ordering a first, when it should return 1
Nothing; returning -1 there puts the empty report first

choices: It throws, as it reads the last update of an empty array
It returns 0, leaving the two reports in their original order
It returns -1, ordering a first, when it should return 1
Nothing; returning -1 there puts the empty report first

items.explanation: The comparator returns -1 if a has no updates (a first, correct) but also -1 if b has none, which puts a first again. The second check should return 1. Such an inconsistent comparator makes the order depend on the engine's sort algorithm, so empty reports are not reliably first; that check returns before the last-update read, so nothing throws.

items.prompt: createStatusReport gets a pageId the workspace owns, plus page component ids that belong to a DIFFERENT page of the same workspace. What does it throw?

choices.text: ForbiddenError, as the components belong to another workspace
NotFoundError, because the components were looked up by pageId
ConflictError, because the components' page differs from pageId
Nothing; the report is linked to whichever page the components use

choices: ForbiddenError, as the components belong to another workspace
NotFoundError, because the components were looked up by pageId
ConflictError, because the components' page differs from pageId
Nothing; the report is linked to whichever page the components use

items.explanation: After the page lookup, validatePageComponentIds checks the ids against the workspace and returns their page. If validated.pageId is not null and differs from input.pageId, the service throws ConflictError('pageId ... does not match the page ... of the selected components.'). Same-workspace components are not forbidden, and the report keeps input.pageId.

items.prompt: A status-page component of type 'static' has incidents on record for the same monitor id. Which incidents does getEvents add for it?

choices.text: Only unresolved incidents, shown with an error status on the page
Only incidents whose monitorId matches the component's monitor
None, since incidents are added only when componentType is not static
Every incident from the last 45 days, as for any other component

choices: Only unresolved incidents, shown with an error status on the page
Only incidents whose monitorId matches the component's monitor
None, since incidents are added only when componentType is not static
Every incident from the last 45 days, as for any other component

items.explanation: The whole incidents block is wrapped in if (componentType !== 'static'); the comment says static components don't have incidents. The 45-day threshold and the monitorId filter apply only inside that block, for monitor-type components.

items.prompt: Kata 2 moves status-report notification off the dashboard's browser `onSuccess` callback. What does the kata say about which layer its test belongs in?

choices.text: It depends on whether the fix is a service, a post-commit job or router code
It belongs in a router test, as notification is part of the tRPC procedure contract
It belongs in a utility test, as dispatch is a pure helper over update ids
It belongs in a dashboard component test that clicks the create button

choices: It depends on whether the fix is a service, a post-commit job or router code
It belongs in a router test, as notification is part of the tRPC procedure contract
It belongs in a utility test, as dispatch is a pure helper over update ids
It belongs in a dashboard component test that clicks the create button

items.explanation: Kata 2 line 58: the design question is whether this should be a new service, a post-commit job, or a router orchestration, and 'the answer changes the test layer'. The premise (line 31) is that notification should no longer depend on the browser's onSuccess, so a dashboard click test is not the target; the kata does not settle on the router or call dispatch a pure utility.

items.prompt: Router Workout 1 pins that a foreign-workspace create is rejected. Its practice extension then considers asserting the error message as well. What does it advise?

choices.text: Never assert the message, as the TRPCError code is the whole public contract
Assert the message only in service tests, since routers rewrite every message
Assert the full message every single time, so that any wording change fails the test
Assert it only if stable, but avoid overfitting to a deliberately generic one

choices: Never assert the message, as the TRPCError code is the whole public contract
Assert the message only in service tests, since routers rewrite every message
Assert the full message every single time, so that any wording change fails the test
Assert it only if stable, but avoid overfitting to a deliberately generic one

items.explanation: Router Workout 1, line 22: assert the error message if stable enough, but avoid overfitting if the message is intentionally generic. That rules out asserting the full wording unconditionally and rules out a blanket ban; the workout says nothing about routers rewriting messages or moving the assertion to service tests.

items.prompt: assertSafeUrlSync is given http://[::ffff:7f00:1]/, the hex form of the IPv4-mapped 127.0.0.1. What does it do?

choices.text: Allows it, since IPv6 hosts skip the private-address checks
Blocks it, since the hex pair is decoded back to 127.0.0.1
Blocks it, since every IPv6 literal is rejected outright
Allows it, since only the dotted ::ffff:127.0.0.1 form is checked

choices: Allows it, since IPv6 hosts skip the private-address checks
Blocks it, since the hex pair is decoded back to 127.0.0.1
Blocks it, since every IPv6 literal is rejected outright
Allows it, since only the dotted ::ffff:127.0.0.1 form is checked

items.explanation: isBlockedHost strips the brackets and calls isBlockedIPv6. For a ::ffff: prefix it first tries the dotted-quad form, then splits the hex pair 7f00:1 and rebuilds 127.0.0.1, which isBlockedIPv4 rejects. The comment notes Node's URL parser turns the dotted form into this hex form. Public IPv6 literals are allowed.

items.prompt: A status report's own status is 'investigating', and its latest update has status 'monitoring'. What event does getEvents produce for it?

choices.text: A success event, as a monitoring update counts as recovery
A degraded event left open, with to kept null until it is resolved
A degraded event that ends at the date of the monitoring update
No event, since only resolved reports appear in the feed

choices: A success event, as a monitoring update counts as recovery
A degraded event left open, with to kept null until it is resolved
A degraded event that ends at the date of the monitoring update
No event, since only resolved reports appear in the feed

items.explanation: Only report.status === 'resolved' gives status 'success'. Otherwise the event is 'degraded' and to is lastUpdate.date when the last update's status is 'resolved' or 'monitoring', else null. So a monitoring update closes the bar's range while the report still shows as degraded.
